story_candidates.title: Intercom lets AI approve code changes: the rules it says keep humans in charge

story_candidates.note: For journalist-ai, categories AI and Corporate. Ready. Intercom's own engineering blog (21 April 2026): say every figure is the company's own statement and was not independently checked. Read the post yourself; give the over 93% agent-driven and over 19% auto-approved with no human reviewer, the rules it names (never forced, any engineer can ask for a human review, the engineer who ships stays accountable, large pull requests not approved, each AI approval labelled and logged), and the pilot and rollout results as the company's (100+ pull requests, zero reverts of AI-approved ones, 497 fully autonomous in four weeks, 0.53% against 5.39% reverts backend and 0.22% against 2.00% frontend, the company adding it does not expect zero to hold); no claim that this is safer than human review. Explain 'pull request', 'revert' and 'sub-agent' in plain words at first use. S80 (CrewAI on human review) is in draft: link it only if it is published when you finish, and repeat none of its content; Zalando's coding-agents article is a different company, link only if useful. 300 to 700 words.
